strengths: Addresses an ambitious, timely, and conceptually appealing direction: enabling unified multi-modal Chain-of-Thought (interleaved visual and textual reasoning/state transitions) within a single autoregressive model.

Proposes a sensible hierarchical conceptual decomposition: separating macro-level task planning and synthesis from micro-level execution formulated as an MDP with attention masking to limit sequence length and memory footprint.
Demonstrates solid experimental numbers on image editing benchmarks (KRIS and RISE) compared to the base BAGEL model and open-source baselines.
weaknesses: Premature manuscript state with missing and promised components: The title itself includes '[Version 0.2: For Nano-Banana Like Generation]', and Section 3.3/B.2 explicitly defers Reinforcement Learning details ('Further details on the reinforcement learning setup will be provided in a future version of this work'). Sections 6 and C similarly defer core aspects ('We will detail the data distribution in the future').

Missing ablation studies: Despite introducing multiple interacting components (macro attention masks, micro MDP attention masks, 4 auxiliary training objectives, and hierarchical decomposition), there are no quantitative ablations showing the contribution or necessity of each part.

Methodological inconsistency between proposal and execution: While Section 3.1 introduces three macro planning mechanisms (Sequential, Parallel, Progressive Refinement), Section 6 admits that Parallel and Progressive refinement are not implemented or working stably, rendering the conceptual scope narrower than advertised.

Limited evaluation scope: Despite motivating the work with visual reasoning (e.g., geometric analysis, navigation, middle-school level spatial reasoning), the evaluation is restricted entirely to generative and editing benchmarks (GenEval, WISE, GEdit-Bench, RISE, KRIS). The model's reasoning capabilities on standard multi-modal understanding/reasoning benchmarks (e.g., MathVista, MMBench, MMMU) are not evaluated.

Repetitive qualitative artifacts: In Figure S3, the first four rows show the exact same textual prompt ('From a satellite image...') and identical text decomposition plans across repeated rows with near-identical outputs, suggesting incomplete or poorly curated supplementary materials.

strengths: The paper tackles an important and ambitious problem: extending Chain-of-Thought (CoT) reasoning to unified multimodal models that interleave image understanding and generation within a single autoregressive framework.

The two-level hierarchical architecture (Macro-level for high-level planning and Micro-level framed as an MDP with self-reflection) is well-motivated by cognitive principles and addresses the severe context-length bottlenecks of multimodal generation.

The attention masking design—masking out fine-grained micro-level steps from the macro planner and enforcing local Markov dependencies during micro-level self-reflection—is an intuitive approach to controlling sequence length and computational overhead.
The empirical results on reasoning-centric image generation (WISE) and image editing (KRIS, RISE) benchmarks demonstrate noticeable improvements over the baseline BAGEL model.
weaknesses: The manuscript is clearly an incomplete working draft. The title explicitly includes '[Version 0.2: For Nano-Banana Like Generation]', and multiple sections state that essential details are deferred to future versions (e.g., Sec. 3.3 and Appendix B.2: 'Further details on the reinforcement learning setup will be provided in a future version of this work'; Appendix C: 'We will detail the data distribution in the future'; and Section D is an empty header).

It is unclear whether reinforcement learning / DPO was actually employed in the reported benchmark experiments (Tables 1–5), as the paper defers RL details to future work and only provides 'Uni-CoT Init' vs. 'Uni-CoT' without specifying the exact training pipeline used for the evaluated checkpoints.

There are virtually no ablation studies validating the core design choices. Specifically, there is no quantitative ablation demonstrating the impact of the macro attention mask, the micro attention mask, the MDP formulation, or the number of reflection steps versus computational cost / memory footprint.

The claims regarding computational efficiency (e.g., training on 8 A100 GPUs) are not benchmarked against standard full-attention or non-hierarchical baselines in terms of wall-clock training time, peak GPU memory, or inference latency.

Formatting and structural issues are evident throughout the document, such as duplicate table numbers (both Macro and Micro tables are labeled as 'Table S3' in the Appendix) and unresolved textual references.

strengths: Timely and ambitious direction: Extending Chain-of-Thought reasoning to unified vision-language generative models (using BAGEL) that alternate between textual reasoning and visual state transitions.

The two-level hierarchical reasoning formulation (Macro-Level CoT for high-level planning and Micro-Level CoT for subtask execution via an MDP formulation) is an intuitive design to mitigate the explosive token context in multimodal autoregressive models.

Comprehensive qualitative and quantitative experiments across multiple image generation and editing benchmarks (GenEval, WISE, GEdit-Bench, KRIS, RISE), showing solid improvements over the BAGEL baseline.
weaknesses: Incomplete submission and draft-like state: The manuscript explicitly marks itself as '[Version 0.2]' in the title and repeatedly defers key technical components to future versions (e.g., Section 3.3 and Appendix B.2 state that details of the RL/DPO framework will be provided in a future release; Appendix C states that dataset distribution details are deferred). This makes the current manuscript incomplete for conference publication.

Lack of essential ablation studies: The paper lacks systematic ablations dissecting its core architectural claims. It remains unclear how much the macro and micro attention masks contribute, the impact of the MDP formulation versus standard full-context attention, the effect of varying the number of reflection rounds, or the necessity of each auxiliary loss objective.

Missing computational efficiency and latency analysis: The paper emphasizes solving the severe computational burden of generating ~9,000 visual tokens per reasoning step, yet it provides no wall-clock training times, inference latency measurements, or memory footprint comparisons against standard single-step or unmasked generation.

Factual and presentation inaccuracies: The paper attributes 'Nano-Banana' to Google (Section 4.5 and Figure 6), whereas reference [44] simply points to a third-party website with no apparent Google affiliation. Additionally, there are editorial errors such as duplicate table numbering (two different tables titled 'Table S3' on page 16).

strengths: Compelling and timely problem formulation: Extending Chain-of-Thought to generate explicit intermediate visual states is severely bottlenecked by token explosion (~9,000 visual tokens per step), which causes quadratic computational overhead and training instability. The paper targets this core challenge directly.

Sound and elegant technical solution: Decomposing reasoning into macro-level planning/summarization and micro-level MDP-guided self-reflection with tailored attention masks theoretically and empirically lowers token interaction complexity from O(T^2) to near-linear O(T).

Comprehensive empirical evaluation: The proposed framework is evaluated across diverse tasks including reasoning-driven image generation (WISE, GenEval), visual understanding (Jigsaw-R1, MMBench, MathVista, MMMU), and image editing (KRIS, RISE, GEdit-Bench), demonstrating consistent benefits.

Strong ablations and model generality: The authors validate the impact of both macro- and micro-reasoning components, examine training efficiency/loss dynamics, and verify architectural transferability by successfully applying Uni-CoT to a different base model (BLIP3o).
weaknesses: Modest gains on standard multimodal understanding benchmarks: On general VQA/knowledge benchmarks (e.g., MMMU changes from 52.8 to 52.7; MathVista from 73.1 to 73.3), the performance improvement over the BAGEL baseline is minimal, indicating the primary gains are restricted to visual state manipulation/puzzle tasks (Jigsaw-R1) and generative editing.

Heavy reliance on proprietary models for data curation: The 31k-sample multi-modal CoT dataset relies on distillation/trajectories generated by GPT-4o and BAGEL-Think without explicit human quality audits or filtering statistics to evaluate synthetic hallucination rates.

Lack of wall-clock runtime / GPU memory benchmarking: While token-interaction counts and theoretical complexity are analyzed in Section 4.5, reporting end-to-end wall-clock latency and peak GPU memory savings during both training and multi-step inference would further strengthen the computational efficiency claims.

Minor presentation and rendering glitches: In Figure 5 (MSE loss comparison) and Figure S5, axis labels and legends suffer from font rendering issues/garbled characters in the PDF, which should be polished.

strengths: Addresses an important and timely problem: mitigating the prohibitive token-length and computational bottleneck of step-wise multi-modal chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning.

The hierarchical macro-micro formulation—coupling high-level task decomposition with Markovian micro-level self-reflection enforced via structured attention masking—is technically sound and provides a clean way to reduce attention overhead.

Comprehensive empirical evaluation covering diverse tasks, including image generation (GenEval, WISE), image understanding (MMMU, MathVista, Jigsaw-R1), and reasoning-driven image editing (GEdit, KRIS, RISE).
Good demonstration of architectural generality, showing successful transfer of the proposed micro-CoT self-reflection mechanism from BAGEL to BLIP3o.
weaknesses: Performance gains on general multi-modal understanding benchmarks (e.g., MME, MMMU, MathVista, MMBench) are marginal compared to the base model BAGEL (e.g., 52.8 vs 52.7 on MMMU, 73.1 vs 73.3 on MathVista), with major gains concentrated mostly on synthetic/perception-heavy benchmarks like Jigsaw-R1.

The connection between the theoretical complexity reduction and practical inference implementation could be clarified, particularly regarding how KV caching is managed (e.g., whether KV caches for masked tokens are explicitly evicted) during autoregressive decoding.

High reliance on proprietary LLM/VLM pipelines (GPT-4o) for synthetic data generation and trajectory curation, which may introduce distillation biases and limit reproducibility without releasing the complete curated trajectory dataset.
The stopping criterion and threshold tuning for the micro-level self-reflection loop during inference are briefly described without sufficient sensitivity analysis.

strengths: Compelling Motivation: Combining multi-modal understanding and generation within a unified step-wise reasoning loop is an important problem. The paper clearly identifies a fundamental bottleneck: the massive token footprint of interleaved images (thousands of tokens per visual state) makes naive autoregressive quadratic attention computationally intractable.

Well-Motivated Technical Formulation: Structuring reasoning into a macro planner/summarizer and micro-level Markov Decision Process (MDP) operators with custom attention masking is a principled approach to reduce attention overhead and prevent long-context degradation.

Comprehensive Benchmark Coverage: The method is evaluated across a broad spectrum of tasks, including text-to-image generation (GenEval, WISE), reasoning-informed image editing (GEdit-Bench, RISE, KRIS), and visual understanding/puzzles (Jigsaw-R1, MME, MMMU).
Generality Across Backbones: The authors validate the applicability of the approach on both BAGEL and BLIP3o architectures, demonstrating positive transfer across different unified model families.
weaknesses: Marginal Impact on General Understanding Benchmarks: While the method shows strong gains on visually structured puzzles (Jigsaw-R1) and image generation/editing, the improvements on standard visual understanding benchmarks (MME, MMMU, MathVista, MMBench in Table 3) are negligible or within noise (e.g., MMMU drops from 52.8 to 52.7, MathVista changes from 73.1 to 73.3). This suggests the unified CoT framework currently benefits generative and perception-rearrangement tasks much more than cognitive multi-modal reasoning.

Heavy Reliance on GPT-4o Distillation: The curated 30K dataset and multi-step trajectories rely extensively on GPT-4o for prompt expansion, subtask decomposition, evaluation scores, and refinement instructions. It remains unclear how much of the performance gain stems from distillation of proprietary model heuristics versus genuine architectural benefits of unified multi-modal CoT.

Lack of Practical Wall-Clock Latency and Memory Analysis: Although theoretical token-interaction counts are analyzed in Section 4.5 and Figure 4, the paper lacks empirical wall-clock generation times, memory footprints, and sampling overhead during inference. Because generating multiple intermediate images via diffusion/flow matching remains inherently slow, evaluating the practical runtime trade-offs of multi-step visual generation is critical.

Confounding Fine-Tuning Gains: In Table 1 and Table 2, the 'Uni-CoT w/o CoT' baseline (fine-tuned without reasoning) already provides noticeable gains over the baseline model BAGEL, indicating that a substantial portion of the performance improvement comes from dataset domain adaptation rather than the multi-modal CoT reasoning alone.

Presentation and Citation Anomalies: The paper contains several unpolished citations with missing authors or dates (e.g., 'Lu et al.', 'Zhang et al.', 'Liu et al.' in the main text and references), as well as unexplained baselines in figures (such as 'GPT-5' referenced in Figure S4 without explanation or attribution).
